sources.title: UK ETS technical guidance and tools
facts: DESNZ collection links Monitoring and Reporting Regulation guidance, free-allocation guidance, reporting templates and current scheme tools.
Guidance, factors and templates define calculation/reporting controls but do not by themselves establish an observed parcel emission.

sources.title: UK ETS technical guidance: Monitoring and Reporting Regulation 2018
facts: DESNZ MRR guidance covers uncertainty assessments, biomass reporting, data-flow controls, sampling and voluntary waste MRV.
A monitoring method or uncertainty rule is a measurement contract, not an emissions observation without underlying activity or measured data.

sources.title: UK ETS Waste quarterly data report template Q2
facts: DESNZ provides the quarter-2 template for waste operators participating in the voluntary MRV period.
A blank reporting template or reporting obligation is not an observed emissions result.

sources.title: Voluntary MRV period for EfW and waste incineration detailed guidance
facts: Environment Agency guidance describes the preparatory voluntary MRV-only period for eligible energy-from-waste and waste-incineration installations.
Participation or future UK ETS scope does not itself prove a physical emissions quantity for a site or parcel.

sources.title: Landfill methane measurement and metrics
facts: Environment Agency research assesses methods for measuring landfill methane emissions and their possible regulatory use.
A research method can support site measurement when applied to a specific survey, but the publication itself is not a parcel observation.

sources.title: Landfill methane measurement and metrics summary
facts: The Environment Agency summary discusses methane measurement surveys, methane collection efficiency and representative operating conditions.
A site survey result has measurement meaning only for the surveyed landfill and conditions and must not be transferred to an unrelated parcel.

sources.title: UK ETS aviation how to comply
facts: Aircraft operators monitor in-scope aviation CO2 and submit verified annual emissions reports under UK ETS.
Aircraft-operator or flight emissions are aviation-activity data and are not land-parcel emissions.

sources.title: Participating in the UK ETS
facts: The current UK ETS overview distinguishes installation, aviation and maritime obligations and notes maritime inclusion from 1 July 2026.
Scheme participation, surrender obligations and allowances are compliance constructs rather than independent physical emissions measurements.

sources.title: UK ETS installations how to comply detailed guidance
facts: Environment Agency and DESNZ guidance requires installations to monitor reportable emissions under an approved plan and submit verified annual reports.
Verified installation totals remain installation-scoped and require explicit geometry binding before any parcel attribution.

sources.title: UK ETS hospital or small emitters how to comply
facts: The guidance covers HSE permit compliance and monitoring/reporting requirements under the UK ETS.
HSE status, targets or permit obligations are not themselves measured parcel emissions.

sources.title: Environment Agency greenhouse gas emissions charging scheme
facts: The Environment Agency publication sets current charges for permits, emissions monitoring plans, subsistence, registry administration and related UK ETS activities.
A regulatory fee or charge category is monetary administration data and cannot proxy physical emissions.

sources.title: Environment Agency GHG charging scheme 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027
facts: The 2026-27 scheme specifies regulatory charges including new maritime emissions-monitoring-plan and subsistence charges.
Charge amounts and fee liability are not greenhouse-gas quantities.

sources.title: Environment Agency GHG charge tables 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2027
facts: The tables publish current monetary charges for installation, aviation, maritime and registry regulatory activities.
Fee tables must remain separated from physical emissions, allowances and measured activity data.

sources.title: Environmental permitting landfill sector technical guidance
facts: Environment Agency collection links landfill gas, surface-emission, flare, engine and monitoring technical guidance.
Technical guidance describes methods and permit expectations but is not a numeric site observation until applied to monitored data.

sources.title: Landfill operators environmental permits
facts: The Environment Agency manual covers landfill gas management, monitoring, reporting, restoration and permit compliance.
A permit manual provides operational requirements and cannot be used as a parcel emissions value.

sources.title: Landfill operators monitor and report performance
facts: Environment Agency guidance requires landfill monitoring and describes methane surface-flux monitoring for capped biodegradable-waste cells.
A measured site-zone flux can be real emissions evidence for that monitored zone, but it is not automatically a cadastral parcel total.

sources.title: Landfill operators manage landfill gas
facts: Environment Agency guidance covers collection, extraction, utilisation, flaring, monitoring and minimisation of landfill gas.
Collected, flared or generated gas is not identical to uncontrolled atmospheric methane emissions and requires the correct system boundary.

sources.title: Landfill operators develop and maintain management plans
facts: The guidance requires landfill gas monitoring/sampling plans and, where required, reporting of annual methane generation rates.
A modelled generation rate, monitoring plan and actual measured release are distinct evidence types.

sources.title: Control and monitor emissions for your environmental permit
facts: Environment Agency guidance distinguishes point-source and fugitive emissions and requires permit-specific monitoring where applicable.
Permit limits and monitoring requirements are constraints; only actual monitoring results provide observed emissions evidence.

sources.title: Monitoring stack emissions standards for continuous monitoring and sampling
facts: Environment Agency guidance describes continuous and periodic stack monitoring, long-term sampling, biogenic CO2 methods and predictive emissions monitoring systems.
Measured stack concentration or modelled PEMS output requires flow, averaging period and system-boundary context before conversion to an annual parcel total.

sources.title: IED environmental permits issued 2026 A to F
facts: Environment Agency collection lists 2026 Industrial Emissions Directive permit decisions for operators A to F.
A permit decision establishes facility and regulatory provenance but is not an emissions measurement.

sources.title: IED environmental permits issued 2026 G to L
facts: Environment Agency collection lists 2026 Industrial Emissions Directive permit decisions for operators G to L.
Permit issue, variation or surrender metadata must remain distinct from observed facility emissions.

sources.title: IED environmental permits issued 2026 M to R
facts: Environment Agency collection lists 2026 Industrial Emissions Directive permit decisions for operators M to R.
A permit collection can support facility identity/currentity but cannot supply an emissions quantity without a separate monitoring dataset.

sources.title: IED environmental permits issued 2026 S to Z
facts: Environment Agency collection lists 2026 Industrial Emissions Directive permit decisions for operators S to Z, including July 2026 entries.
Decision/currentity evidence is not a greenhouse-gas observation unless a referenced monitoring result independently supports it.

sources.title: Specified generator apply for an environmental permit
facts: Environment Agency guidance covers environmental permits, emission-limit compliance verification and decarbonisation-readiness information for specified generators.
Permit eligibility, screening or decarbonisation readiness is not a measured greenhouse-gas emission for a parcel.
